input: Convert old VHS home movies to digital files

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of tapes and total runtime directly affects time, cost, and method chosen — a single tape is trivial; dozens of tapes may require a professional service or dedicated hardware.
Whether the user has a budget for a paid service vs. doing it themselves with borrowed or purchased equipment determines the entire approach.
Whether they already own or have access to a VHS player and capture hardware is the single most immediate blocker to getting started.
The desired output format and quality level (e.g., MP4 for easy sharing vs. lossless for archiving) shapes every technical decision downstream.
Knowing who the final files are for — personal archive, sharing with family, a memorial video — changes priorities around labeling, editing, and distribution.
The physical condition of the tapes matters greatly; tapes that are degraded, mouldy, or very old may require professional restoration rather than a simple home capture.
Understanding whether 'done' means raw captures only, or also organized, edited, and distributed files, defines the full scope of the project.

gold.taskTitle: Convert VHS home movies to digital files
gold.taskDescription: Transfer a collection of old VHS tapes containing home movies into digital video files.

questions.title: How many VHS tapes do you need to convert?
questions.description: The total number of tapes determines whether a DIY setup, a local service, or a mail-in service is most practical and cost-effective.

questions.title: Do you have a working VHS player and capture device?
questions.description: Knowing what equipment is already on hand identifies the immediate first blocker and whether any purchases or rentals are needed before starting.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: A tight budget may favour a DIY approach with borrowed gear, while a more flexible budget opens up professional mail-in or local digitisation services.

questions.title: What file format and quality level do you need?
questions.description: Casual sharing calls for compressed MP4 files, while long-term archiving may require higher-quality or lossless formats — this shapes all technical decisions.

questions.title: Who will the final digital files be shared with or used by?
questions.description: Personal archiving, sharing with extended family, or creating a tribute video each require different levels of organisation, editing, and distribution planning.

questions.title: What is the current physical condition of the tapes?
questions.description: Tapes that are old, mouldy, sticky, or showing playback issues may need professional restoration before or during digitisation, changing the recommended approach entirely.

questions.title: Should the files be edited and organised, or just raw captures?
questions.description: Defining whether 'done' means raw footage only, or also trimmed, labelled, and delivered files, sets the true end goal and effort required for the project.
